newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech FinMin approves opening closed Harvard funds.
newsitem.headline: Czech FinMin approves opening closed Harvard funds.

text.p: The Czech Finance Ministry on Tuesday said it had approved an application by Harvard Capital and Consulting (HC&C) to open its closed-ended mutual investment funds.
"It (the application to open the funds) has been approved. It was signed this morning," ministry spokewoman Ludmila Nutilova told Reuters.
In mid-January, HC&C applied to the Finance Ministry to transform its closed-end unit trusts into open-end funds in order to "extend investment opportunities."

But in March, the ministry rejected Harvard's original application to open the funds, which were created during the second wave of the government's voucher privatisation scheme which ended in 1995, saying unit holders of the funds needed to be protected.
Harvard immediately re-applied, and said it had met the requirements of the ministry, which have not been disclosed.
Harvard officials were not imediately available for comment.
HC&C has said that if the measure was approved, it would offer to buy out shareholders from the funds at a price equal to the net asset value per share.
Harvard currently has some 12 funds publicly-traded on the Prague Stock Exchange. It was not clear if the approval would allow all of the Harvard funds to open.
